key_insight: Known fault positions are worth more than unknown ones. Herding them into one RS symbol makes k weak bits cost one erasure instead of k symbol errors.
killer_doubt: Herding still stores each weak-bit position (~10 b), the cost of bit-fix pointer repair that fixes it outright. A 512-input Benes setting is ~4,400 bits. VRT cells escape boot maps.
decisive_experiment: Software, ~$50k: take DRAM Bender fail maps from 20 DDR5 dies at 2-4x refresh interval. At equal residual FIT, compare check plus metadata bits per codeword for herding, erasure RS and bit-fix/ArchShield, including VRT churn.
prior_art: Bamboo ECC symbol layout (Kim, Sullivan, Erez, HPCA 2015); bit-fix (Wilkerson, ISCA 2008); ArchShield fault map (Nair, ISCA 2013); AVATAR for VRT [training knowledge].

key_insight: Winding gives thousands of layers and volumetric packing without a per-tier process, on roll-to-roll web lines instead of wafer fabs.
killer_doubt: Winding shares no patterning, so cost/bit is R2R $/m2 over bits/m2: ~20 GB/m2 at 1 um rules is ~$2-10/GB versus $1.48 (estimate). Micron-scale TFTs and m-long lines miss 100 ns.
decisive_experiment: Paper model first (~$20k): $/GB and line RC for a wound R2R IGZO array at 1-2 um rules. Only if positive, wind a 100-turn test roll and measure per-turn end-face contact yield after laser-patterned Schoop spray.
prior_art: Rolled-up nanomembrane capacitors and micro-batteries (O. G. Schmidt, IFW Dresden); wound film capacitors; R2R flexible ICs (PragmatIC) [training knowledge]. No wound memory found.

key_insight: Local majority rules (Toom) can keep stored data stable with no global decoder, so in principle correction runs inside refresh for a few gates per column.
killer_doubt: Local 2D codes are low-rate: 8x8 row/column parity costs 25% check cells versus ~2% for 512-bit BCH. Refresh opens one row, not a 2D neighbourhood.
decisive_experiment: Simulation, ~$30k: Monte Carlo of Toom-style local decoding against DDR5-style ECS scrub with on-die SEC or t=4 BCH, at raw BER 1e-5 to 1e-3, equal check-bit overhead and equal refresh energy.
prior_art: Toom's rule (1980); Gacs reliable cellular automata; DDR5/HBM3 on-die ECC with error check-and-scrub during refresh windows [training knowledge].

key_insight: Linear check bits work as a stored fingerprint: matching a predicted line's syndrome reads a 1/8-width subarray and returns one bit instead of 512.
killer_doubt: The requester must already hold the predicted line, which is a cache. Compression flags already catch zero or uniform lines. DRAM-miss value locality is likely under 30% (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Trace study, ~$40k: on SPEC, graph and LLM-serving LLC-miss traces, measure the misses a <=64 KB last-value or stride predictor gets right beyond zero/uniform lines. Kill below 10%.
prior_art: Load value prediction (Lipasti, 1996); silent-store detection (Lepak and Lipasti); zero-line flags in compressed memory, e.g. Compresso [training knowledge].

key_insight: Spread-spectrum storage turns a dead cell into small noise across many bits instead of a hard error, the holographic trade.
killer_doubt: Each cell holds a 129-level Walsh sum to carry one bit: ~5-bit analog precision (sigma under ~2.5 levels) buys 1 bit/cell, ~5x below direct MLC plus ECC.
decisive_experiment: Arithmetic only (~$10k): capacity per cell for N=64 Walsh spreading against 4-level MLC plus BCH, on a measured gain-cell noise and drift distribution.
prior_art: Holographic and CDMA-style storage; Hadamard spreading for error resilience (this study's I-08644 and I-10422, both dropped) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Pairwise lot splits give a cheap running rank of chambers, so a fab can keep depreciated tools on tolerant layers instead of replacing them.
killer_doubt: Fabs already log every wafer's chamber path; a mixed-effects commonality model on all lots beats Elo's pairwise updates. Claimed gain is only +1-3% yield, and testing needs fab data.
decisive_experiment: With one fab partner's anonymised chamber-path and bit-fail history (public SECOM data as a stand-in), compare Elo and a mixed-effects commonality model at predicting next-month yield by chamber. ~$100k.
prior_art: Commonality analysis and tool dispatch in PDF Solutions Exensio, KLA and Applied SmartFactory; chamber matching; Bradley-Terry ranking [training knowledge].

key_insight: Multi-way swap cycles could clear allocation mismatches (DDR4 vs DDR5, LPDDR vs RDIMM) without cash price discovery.
killer_doubt: Unlike kidneys, DRAM can be sold: brokers and the spot market already clear surplus for cash. Gain is capped by an unverified 5-10% mismatched inventory; allocation terms often bar transfer.
decisive_experiment: Survey 30-50 OEMs, ODMs and distributors for mismatched holdings and transfer limits. Then run a 3-month swap pilot with a distributor as altruistic donor. Kill if cleared volume is under 1% of participants' DRAM spend. ~$150k.
prior_art: Barter-exchange clearing (Abraham, Blum, Sandholm, EC 2007); component brokers and excess-inventory marketplaces [training knowledge].

key_insight: Supply elasticity is the scarce good. Capacity that can be switched on in weeks has real option value against a 4x price spike.
killer_doubt: Tier wafers still need front-end fab time, so stockpiled base and tier wafers are wafer-bank inventory. Bonding adds weeks, not supply. Modular tier-bonded DRAM does not exist (0 products).
decisive_experiment: Desk model, ~$40k: price a capacity option on 2016-2026 DRAM contract prices against the carrying cost of wafer-bank inventory and existing LTA prepayments. Kill if the premium is below carrying cost.
prior_art: Memory makers' wafer and die banks; hyperscaler long-term agreements and prepayments; YMTC Xtacking and Kioxia CBA wafer bonding [training knowledge].

key_insight: Most bitlines in an activation carry ample signal. Spending large, trimmed amplifiers only on the marginal ~1% could cut sense-amp area and energy.
killer_doubt: Flagging suspect columns needs ECC decode in the sense-amp stripe on ~8k bits per chip every activation. If ECC finds the errors, re-sensing is moot. Pool muxes load bitlines.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus layout on a DRAM-like PDK proxy, ~$60k: min-size isolated latch, ECC decoder area for a 1 KB page, and mux load on bitline signal, compared with an offset-cancelling BLSA.
prior_art: Offset-cancellation bitline sense amplifiers (Samsung, SK hynix); DDR5 on-die ECC; this study's I-11559 ECC-paid capacitor [training knowledge].

key_insight: Bootstrapping the inner access device's far terminal to the storage node removes Vds-driven subthreshold leakage, the classic electrometer guard.
killer_doubt: DRAM's <=13 fA tail is GIDL and trap-assisted junction leakage, which nulling Vds does not touch. Three devices plus a follower supply cost ~2x area; IGZO is ~1e3x lower natively.
decisive_experiment: As for I-02778: a 28/40 nm MPW (~$150k) with plain and guarded cells. Measure 85 C retention tails and split leakage into subthreshold, GIDL and junction parts.
prior_art: Leakage-compensated 4T gain cells (Teman, Meinerzhagen, Burg, ~2014); T-switch sample-and-hold; this study's I-02778, dropped [training knowledge].

key_insight: Gates that exist when epitaxy ends would delete the replacement gate-all-around module in lateral cavities, the hardest step of the 3D DRAM access transistor.
killer_doubt: Pinch-off fixes the junction field near ~3 V/a: ~1.3 MV/cm for a 50 nm channel, in GIDL/trap-tunnelling range. Holding ~0.6 MV/cm needs ~100 nm channels, roughly doubling tier pitch (estimate).
decisive_experiment: TCAD first (~$30k): double-gate JFET pinch-off and BTBT/TAT leakage at 85 C versus channel thickness. If a <=40 nm channel holds <1 fA, grow a 3-tier in-situ boron-doped Si/SiGe stack with a partner; measure Ioff and SIMS (~$400k).
prior_art: In-situ doped Si/SiGe JFETs in a logic patent; Si/SiGe GAA 3D DRAM (Samsung, imec; IMW/VLSI 2023) (via search snippet). No JFET 3D DRAM cell found.

key_insight: In 3D the plate can be cut without touching transistor tiers. An 8-cell plate strip as the sense node, bitline clamped, sees ~2-3 fF instead of ~30 fF.
killer_doubt: Plate-line sensing was patented for planar DRAM and never shipped. One sense path per 8 cells costs array efficiency; vertical strips span all ~100 tiers unless cut every 8.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus layout (~$50k): 8- and 16-tier plate-segmented lateral array; sense pitch, energy per activation and disturb on unselected floating nodes over 1e12 accesses. Then an IGZO 8-cell test strip on a university run (~$250k).
prior_art: Planar DRAM patents: sensing via plate line (US6201730); segmented plate lines to sense amps (US6477098, US6246604) (via search snippet). No 3D version found.
